texts.preamble: Shanthi vs Royal Sun Alli Insn Co Ltd on 11 August, 2025 Kabc020000042019 Kabc020000052019 Kabc020056972019 Before The Motor Accident Claims Tribunal Court of Small Causes, Bengaluru. Dated This The 11th Day Of August 2025 Present: Sri.B.S.HONNASWAMY (B.A., Ll.M) Vii Addl. Scj and Acjm, Member, Mact-3, Bengaluru. M.V.C.No.3/2019, M.V.C.No.4/2019 and M.V.C.No.1231/2019 Petitioners in : 01. Sri . Anjinappa, Mvc 3/2019 S/o Muniyappa, Aged about 52 years, 02. Anitha.A, D/o Anjinappa, Aged about 32 years, (Scch-3) 2 M.V.C.No.3/2019 c/w M.V.C.No.4/2019, M.V.C.No.1231/2019 03. Shruthi.A, D/o Anjinappa, Aged about 27 years, 04.
texts.facts: 03 . The brief facts of the case of the petitioners is as under: That on 04.12.2018 at about 11.50 p.m, the deceased persons and petitioner were proceeding in a (SCCH-3) 7 M.V.C.No.3/2019 c/w M.V.C.No.4/2019, M.V.C.No.1231/2019 Maruti Omni Car bearing No.KA-03-MJ-2959 and the same was driven by its driver on the left side of the road from Bengaluru towards Devanahalli, when they reached near Kanmangala Palya Gate, at tha time a Innova Car bearing No.KA-03-NB-9119 which belongs to respondent No.2, driven by its driver in rash and negligent manner, at high speed and dashed behind the Maruti Omni Car in which they were proceeding. Due to which Venkatesh and Sundar.S sustained grievous injuries and died on the spot and petitioner in M.V.C.No.1231/2019 sustained grievous injuries. Prior to the accident the deceased in M.V.C.No.3/2019 was hale and healthy and was aged about 28 years and was doing Event Management and Flower decorations work and earning Rs.20,000/- p.m and was the only bread winner in his family. Due to accidental injuries, the petitioners are put to great financial loss and mental agony. Prior to the accident the deceased in M.V.C.No.4/2019 was hale and healthy and was aged about 22 years and was doing Event Management and Flower decorations work, apart from he was working as Driver under one Chand Pasha and earning (SCCH-3) 8 M.V.C.No.3/2019 c/w M.V.C.No.4/2019, M.V.C.No.1231/2019 Rs.20,000/- p.m and was the only bread winner in his family. Prior to the accident the petitioner in M.V.C.No.1231/2019 was hale and healthy and was aged about 23 years and was doing Flower decorator work and earning Rs.20,000/- p.m and he has incurred Rs.1,50,000/- towards treatment, medicines, conveyance and nourishment. Due to accidental Shanthi vs Royal Sun Alli Insn Co Ltd on 11 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156673867/ 5 injuries, he is unable to do his work and his entire family are put to great financial loss and mental agony. The accident is occurred due to rash and negligent driving of driver of offending Innova Car and in this regard the BIAL Traffic Police have registered a case against driver of the offending car in Crime No.173/2018 for the offences punishable U/Sec 279, 338 of IPC. The respondent No.1 is the RC Owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the said offending vehicle, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation of Rs.25,00,000/-, Rs.25,00,000/- and Rs.10,00,000/- respectively to the petitioners together with interest at the rate of 12% p.a with costs. (SCCH-3) 9 M.V.C.No.3/2019 c/w M.V.C.No.4/2019, M.V.C.No.1231/2019 04. On service of notice, the respondents No.1 and 2 have appeared before the tribunal through their counsels, but only the respondent No.1 has filed objections in all the petitions. Later the counsel for the petitioners have filed application to implead respondents No.3 to 8 as they are all Charge sheeted accused. Later they are appeared before the tribunal, but not filed their objections. 05. The respondent No.1 in its objections has denied the entire case of the petitioners and further denied age, income, occupation of deceased persons and petitioner and manner of accident, involvement of the vehicle, expenses incurred by the petitioners, dependency of the petitioners with the deceased persons and contended that the driver of the offending car was not holding valid and effective driving licence at the time of accident as on the date of accident, the owner of the car has contravened the provisions of M.V. Act and Rules and they committed the breach of terms and conditions of the policy and admits that this respondent has issued policy of insurance in favour of respondent No.2 in respect of Car bearing No. KA-03-NB-9119 and the liability of this respondent if (SCCH-3) 10 M.V.C.No.3/2019 c/w M.V.C.No.4/2019, M.V.C.No.1231/2019 any, is limited to terms and conditions of the policy. The car in question did not involved in the accident nor caused accidental injuries to the petitioner and on the date of accident the car was being driven in a reasonable speed and careful manner and there was no rashness or negligence on the part of the driver of car and the accident occurred due to the negligence on Shanthi vs Royal Sun Alli Insn Co Ltd on 11 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156673867/ 6 the part of the driver of the omni car, in which deceased persons and petitioner were travelling. The petition is bad for non-joinder of proper and necessary parties. The compensation claimed is highly excessive, exaggerated and hence, pray for dismiss the petition with costs against respondent No.1. 06. Based on the aforesaid pleadings, the following issues have been framed by my learned predecessor: - ISSUES IN MVC NO.3/2019 01. By way of rebuttal, the respondent No.1 did not lead evidence inspite of sufficient opportunity has been given.
texts.arguments: In view of the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Pranay Sethi & Others case, the future prospects or additional income should be added to monthly income of the deceased. Since the deceased was a bachelor, it is appropriate to deduct 50% of the income of the deceased towards personal and living expenses of the deceased and then his monthly income would be (17,500 - 8,750) = Rs.8,750/-. In view of the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Pranay Sethi & Others case in respect to loss of consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses, the aforesaid amount should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every 3 years. Accordingly, in the head of loss of consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses, 10% is enhanced for period of every 3 years. In view of the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in Magma General Insurance Company Ltd., V/s Nanu Ram alias Churu Ram reported in (2018) 18 SCC 130, the petitioners No.2 to 5 are entitled for Rs.40,000/- each towards loss of love and affection and petitioners are entitled for Rs.19,500/- each towards loss of estate and funeral expenses and transportation of dead body. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case (SCCH-3) 22 M.V.C.No.3/2019 c/w M.V.C.No.4/2019, M.V.C.No.1231/2019 and noticing the number of dependents and 50% of the income taken into consideration towards the personal and living expenses of the deceased , this Tribunal has placed reliance on ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680 in between National Insurance Co.
